name: sales
description: B2B sales memory: deals, accounts, contacts and reps from the CRM, plus what calls, emails and notes say about them (stakeholders, commitments, objections, competitors, qualification).

deal.description: An opportunity. Ids are deal:<crm id>.

stage.description: The org's own pipeline stages (open enum).

currency.description: The ISO 4217 code of the deal's currency (EUR); its amount is in it, in USD when it names none.

current_tool.description: a tool they use today relevant to the deal, including in-house tools and home-built attempts that failed; keep the key specifics

account.description: A company, or a household in wealth management. Ids are account:<id>.

current_process.description: one step of how they onboard, train or coach reps today, e.g. 'two weeks shadowing a senior rep before taking calls'

product_line.description: a line of business, including the business mix ('mostly commercial accounts') and lines they no longer sell

sales_language.description: a language their reps sell in

contact.description: A person at an account. Ids are contact:<id>.

company.description: The company name on the CRM record, which may name a company that has no account.

stakeholder.description: A contact's part in one deal: an edge with properties. Ids are stakeholder:<deal id>:<contact id>.

rep.description: A seller on our side. Ids are rep:<user id>.

meeting.description: A call or meeting. Ids are meeting:<id>.

commitment.description: Something someone said they would do. Ids are commitment:<id>.

task.description: A to-do in AmpUp or the CRM; its name is the subject. Ids are task:<id>.

status.description: open, completed, dismissed, expired and the like (open enum).

priority.description: How urgent the task is. A CRM's own spellings are stored as one of these (Normal as medium, P0 as high).

source.description: Where the task came from, such as AmpUp or hubspot.

objection.description: A concern a buyer raised. Ids are objection:<id>.

category.description: The org's own objection categories (open enum).

raised_in.description: The meetings it came up in, so counts per meeting work.

competitor.description: Another vendor in the deal. Ids are competitor:<slug>.

coaching_signal.description: An observation about a rep's selling. Ids are coaching_signal:<id>.

channel.description: A chat channel, by its id (channel:C024BE91L).

incident.description: An error tracker's issue: one error grouped across its occurrences. Ids are incident:<org>/<project>/issues/<id>.

issue.description: An issue or ticket, by the id its tracker gives it: issue:<owner>/<repo>#<number> from a code host, issue:<workspace>/<KEY-123> from a tracker.

lead.description: A CRM lead: someone the CRM tracks before they are a contact. Ids are lead:<crm>-<crm id> (lead:hs-42).

company.description: The company name on the lead.

status.description: Its status in the CRM (open enum).

owner.description: Who owns it in the CRM.

person.description: Anyone, by email address: person:<lower-cased email> (person:dana@example.com). The id calls, calendars and emails name people by; a CRM contact, lead or rep with that email is the same person.

company.description: The company they work for, as stated.

pr.description: A merged pull request. Ids are pr:<owner>/<repo>#<number>.

repo.description: A code repository. Ids are repo:<owner>/<repo>.

command.description: A command the team runs in this repository (build, test, deploy, release), quoted exactly, with what it does; a renamed one names the old name too.

convention.description: A rule the team follows in this repository (naming, branches, reviews, style, where things go), as stated.

decision.description: A decision about this repository's code, tooling or process, with who took it when that is said.

slack_user.description: A chat account, by its id (slack_user:U024BE7LH); the person behind it is a person or a rep.

thread.description: A chat thread, as thread:<channel id>:<thread ts>.

topic.description: What an internal meeting or Slack thread is about when it is not one deal: a project, product area or feature, a customer's issue, a process, hiring, an incident. Ids are topic:<slug>, such as topic:notetaker_recording or topic:q4_pricing.

decision.description: A decision taken, with who took it when that is said.

issue.description: A problem raised and not yet resolved.

next_step.description: What someone said happens next, with the owner's name when said.

related_deal.description: Deals or accounts the topic touches, when any.

summary.description: Where it stands, one or two lines, as of the latest discussion.

pipeline_by_stage.title: Open pipeline by stage
pipeline_by_stage.description: Open deals per stage, with their total amount.

objections_by_deal_stage.title: Objections by deal stage
objections_by_deal_stage.description: Objections per stage of the deal they are about.

open_commitments_by_owner.title: Open commitments by owner
open_commitments_by_owner.description: Open or stale commitments per owner.

active_deals.title: Active deals, last 90 days vs the 90 before
active_deals.description: Deals with a meeting in the window.
active_deals.sql: SELECT count(DISTINCT d.value_ref) FILTER (WHERE s.value_ts >= now() - INTERVAL '90 days') AS last_90d, count(DISTINCT d.value_ref) FILTER (WHERE s.value_ts < now() - INTERVAL '90 days' AND s.value_ts >= now() - INTERVAL '180 days') AS prior_90d, array_agg(d.fact_id) FILTER (WHERE s.value_ts >= now() - INTERVAL '90 days') AS fact_ids FROM current d JOIN current s ON s.entity = d.entity WHERE d.predicate = 'deal' AND s.predicate = 'scheduled_at' AND s.value_ts <= now()

coaching_by_skill.title: Coaching signals by skill
coaching_by_skill.description: What coaching observations are about, across reps.

deal_signals.title: Objections and competitors per deal
deal_signals.description: Each deal's objection categories and the competitors named on it, to set against outcomes.
deal_signals.sql: SELECT a.value_ref AS deal, 'objection' AS kind, c.value AS value, array_agg(DISTINCT c.fact_id) AS fact_ids FROM current a JOIN current c ON c.entity = a.entity WHERE a.predicate = 'about' AND c.predicate = 'category' AND a.value_ref LIKE 'deal:%' GROUP BY 1, 2, 3 UNION ALL SELECT entity AS deal, 'competitor' AS kind, value_ref AS value, array_agg(DISTINCT fact_id) AS fact_ids FROM current WHERE predicate = 'competitor' AND entity LIKE 'deal:%' GROUP BY 1, 2, 3

deals_by_competitor.title: Deals by competitor
deals_by_competitor.description: Deals where a competitor is in play.
deals_by_competitor.sql: SELECT value_ref AS competitor, count(DISTINCT entity) AS deals, array_agg(fact_id) AS fact_ids FROM current WHERE predicate = 'competitor' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY deals DESC, competitor

meddpicc_coverage.title: MEDDPICC coverage
meddpicc_coverage.description: Deals per MEDDPICC element confirmed or partly known.
meddpicc_coverage.sql: SELECT replace(predicate, 'meddpicc_', '') AS element, count(*) FILTER (WHERE value = 'confirmed') AS confirmed, count(*) FILTER (WHERE value = 'partial') AS partial, count(*) AS known, array_agg(fact_id) FILTER (WHERE value IN ('confirmed', 'partial')) AS fact_ids FROM current WHERE predicate LIKE 'meddpicc_%' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY confirmed DESC, element

meetings_analyzed.title: Meetings analyzed, last 90 days vs the 90 before
meetings_analyzed.description: Meetings held, by when they were scheduled.
meetings_analyzed.sql: SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE value_ts >= now() - INTERVAL '90 days') AS last_90d, count(*) FILTER (WHERE value_ts < now() - INTERVAL '90 days' AND value_ts >= now() - INTERVAL '180 days') AS prior_90d, array_agg(fact_id) FILTER (WHERE value_ts >= now() - INTERVAL '90 days') AS fact_ids FROM current WHERE predicate = 'scheduled_at' AND value_ts <= now()

objections_trend.title: Objections, last 30 days vs the 30 before
objections_trend.description: Objections raised per category, by when they were recorded.
objections_trend.sql: SELECT value AS category, count(*) FILTER (WHERE valid_from >= now() - INTERVAL '30 days') AS last_30d, count(*) FILTER (WHERE valid_from < now() - INTERVAL '30 days' AND valid_from >= now() - INTERVAL '60 days') AS prior_30d, array_agg(fact_id) FILTER (WHERE valid_from >= now() - INTERVAL '60 days') AS fact_ids FROM current WHERE predicate = 'category' GROUP BY 1 HAVING count(*) FILTER (WHERE valid_from >= now() - INTERVAL '60 days') > 0 ORDER BY last_30d DESC, category

overdue_commitments.title: Overdue commitments by owner
overdue_commitments.description: Open commitments past their due date.
overdue_commitments.sql: SELECT o.value_ref AS owner, count(DISTINCT o.entity) AS overdue, array_agg(DISTINCT d.fact_id) AS fact_ids FROM current o JOIN current s ON s.entity = o.entity JOIN current d ON d.entity = o.entity WHERE o.predicate = 'owner' AND s.predicate = 'status' AND s.value = 'open' AND d.predicate = 'due' AND d.value_ts < now() GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY overdue DESC, owner

stuck_deals.title: What's holding active deals
stuck_deals.description: Per deal with a meeting in the last 90 days, the signals in memory that it is stuck: open objections, overdue commitments, skeptical or opposed stakeholders, no next step, no confirmed champion.
stuck_deals.sql: WITH active AS ( SELECT m.value_ref AS deal, max(s.value_ts) AS last_meeting FROM current m JOIN current s ON s.entity = m.entity WHERE m.entity_type = 'meeting' AND m.predicate = 'deal' AND s.predicate = 'scheduled_at' AND s.value_ts >= now() - INTERVAL '90 days' AND s.value_ts <= now() GROUP BY 1), signals AS ( SELECT a.value_ref AS deal, 'open objection' AS reason, a.fact_id AS fact_id FROM current a JOIN current st ON st.entity = a.entity WHERE a.entity_type = 'objection' AND a.predicate = 'about' AND st.predicate = 'status' AND st.value = 'open' UNION ALL SELECT a.value_ref, 'overdue commitment', a.fact_id FROM current a JOIN current st ON st.entity = a.entity JOIN current du ON du.entity = a.entity WHERE a.entity_type = 'commitment' AND a.predicate = 'about' AND st.predicate = 'status' AND st.value = 'open' AND du.predicate = 'due' AND du.value_ts < now() UNION ALL SELECT a.value_ref, 'skeptical stakeholder', sn.fact_id FROM current a JOIN current sn ON sn.entity = a.entity WHERE a.entity_type = 'stakeholder' AND a.predicate = 'deal' AND sn.predicate = 'stance' AND sn.value IN ('skeptical', 'opposed') UNION ALL SELECT d.deal, 'no next step', CAST(NULL AS VARCHAR) FROM active d WHERE d.deal NOT IN (SELECT entity FROM current WHERE predicate = 'next_step') UNION ALL SELECT d.deal, 'no confirmed champion', CAST(NULL AS VARCHAR) FROM active d WHERE d.deal NOT IN (SELECT entity FROM current WHERE predicate = 'meddpicc_champion' AND value = 'confirmed')) SELECT s.deal, max(o.value_ref) AS owner, array_agg(DISTINCT s.reason) AS reasons, count(DISTINCT s.reason) AS signals, max(a.last_meeting) AS last_meeting, max(am.value_num) AS amount, array_agg(DISTINCT s.fact_id) FILTER (WHERE s.fact_id IS NOT NULL) AS fact_ids FROM signals s JOIN active a ON a.deal = s.deal LEFT JOIN current o ON o.entity = s.deal AND o.predicate = 'owner' LEFT JOIN current am ON am.entity = s.deal AND am.predicate = 'amount' GROUP BY s.deal ORDER BY signals DESC, s.deal

guidance: Know where every deal stands: MEDDPICC coverage, open commitments and objections, and what comes next.

Deals won in a period: count by close_date, which the CRM sets when a deal is won. Deals lost in a period: a lost deal's close_date often keeps its old expected date, so count by when its status changed to lost (find changes with type deal, select ["status"] and that window). When close_date and the status change disagree, say which you counted.

A stakeholder's CRM role is often missing or stale. For who decides, the champion or a blocker, also read passages about the deal (deal context, qualification reviews, calls) and say where they disagree with the CRM.
Tasks are records, not passages: find them with type task, for example where {"rel": "deal", "to": {"id": "deal:<id>"}} and status eq open.

Internal meetings and Slack threads are often about no deal: record them as a topic (project, feature, customer issue, process, incident) with its decisions, open issues and next steps, and link related_deal only when a deal or account is actually named.

A customer's deal or account is the subject of what is said about that customer, even in an internal thread or meeting: write it to deal:<name> or account:<name>, never to a topic named after the customer. A topic is for the team's own work (a feature, a project, a process, an incident).
One person may have several ids: person:<email> from calls, calendars and emails, and contact:, lead: or rep: from the CRM. Search by their email to find them all.
